Q: How to preserve row indices when converting an indexed matrix to a table? A:

Since the values of a matrix do not include its row labels, when converting a matrix to a table, only the values of the matrix will be converted into columns of the table. If you need to ensure that the label columns in the matrix are not lost and become the first column of the table, you need to add them manually.

You can extract the row labels of the matrix using the rowNames() function and append them to the converted table.

correctT = table(m.rowNames()) join table(m)
correctM = matrix(correctT[,1:]).rename!(correctT.Date,correctT.colNames()[1:])

Q: Reverse the states of 2 git commits and rewrite the history A:

An alternative to @jthill's solutions with the plumbing commands read-tree and commit-tree, could be by mixed-resetting to commit B, and then patch-adding the line with 222 with the edit option to commit this single change (commit D). Finally, you can commit the only change left (line 333) and obtain commit E.

# make sure to be on branch feat
git checkout feat

# mixed resetting to commit B
git reset --mixed HEAD~

# stage only the change with 222 with the edit option
git add --patch -- test.txt

# create commit D with only 222
git commit -m "D"

# staging the remaining changes
git add test.txt

# creating commit E with only 333
git commit -m "E"
